newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Friday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Friday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Friday:

Spokesman Patrick Child briefed on the informal ECOFIN Council taking place in Noordwijk, the Netherlands, this week. He said main points on the agenda relating to the EMU would include a detailed calendar and the procedures to be followed in 1998. He said the finance ministers and the central bank governors of the EU would also examine the technical work of transposing into legal texts the political decisions on EMU taken at the Dublin European Council. Child also said the issue of budgetary discipline would be discussed at lunchtime.
Van der Pas said Commissioner Yves-Thibault de Silguy would hold a news conference at 1700/1600 GMT at the press centre in Noordwijk to espress his personal views on the informal Council's agenda.

In answer to a question on the EU's pending decision on a human rights resolution in the United Nations on China and apparent Chinese pressure on France in return for an Airbus contract, van der Pas said it showed the need for a real common foreign security policy and the infrastructure to obtain such policy.
The Commission released the following documents:
- IP/97/262: Food safety: first meeting of the renewed Multidisciplinary Scientific Committee.
- IP/97/269: EU and Japan discuss harbour practices.

- IP/97/270: Humanitarian crisi in Zaire: joint statement by Commissioner Emma Bonino, UN High Commissioner for Refugees Sadako Ogata, UNICEF Executive Director Carol Bellamy and WFP Executive Director Catherine Bertini.
- Memo/97/35: Calendar of the Commissioners activities for the week from April 7 to April 13, 1997.
- Eurostat Memo No2/97: Social protecion in the EU - Rising share of unemployment benefits.
